title: Figma Pricing 2026: Free Plan, Seats and Billing Costs
summary: Figma pricing is per-seat monthly, with rates ranging from $16 (Professional) to $90 (Enterprise). See how different plans affect your team's costs.
body_markdown:
## Right-sizing Figma seats with Activepieces


On Activepieces you can build a scheduled workflow that gathers your seat data and sends the list to a person who approves it before any seat is removed, drawing on 746 integrations, with an MIT-licensed core and unlimited flows on every plan, including free, so cost won't stand in the way of automating this process.


It doesn't lower Figma's price or change what any seat type costs.


Describe the audit in its built-in chat, naming Figma as the source and Slack as the destination, and what comes back is a published flow in your account, the same kind a builder would assemble by hand, running under the same RBAC and audit logs as every other flow, with a run trace that records what each step did on every run.


That limit matters. The tool reports and routes; a person still has to downgrade the seat in Figma's admin settings. Treat it as the thing that makes the audit happen on schedule instead of when someone remembers.


### Scheduled seat audit


Start with a schedule trigger, then a step that pulls the member list and each member's seat type from Figma. Filter for people holding a paid seat with no recent activity, and send that list to the person who owns the bill.


Because the check repeats, a seat assigned during a one-off project doesn't sit unnoticed for a whole billing cycle.


The catch is access. Figma's API and admin-level data are tied to the plan and to your role on it, so confirm your plan exposes member and seat data before you build anything.


If it doesn't, the flow has nothing to read, and a manual export from the admin panel is the fallback.


"Inactive" is your definition, not Figma's: a developer who opens files twice a quarter may be correctly seated, so route the list to a human rather than auto-downgrading.


### Figma comment and handoff alerts without Full seats


People are often given an editor seat only so they can see comments or catch a handoff. That is a common reason for over-seating, and this second use, though smaller, removes it.


A flow that forwards new comments to a Slack channel or an email address lets reviewers respond without holding a seat they otherwise wouldn't need.


The screenshot shows the same pattern with a different trigger: a two-step flow where a Stripe "Payment Failed" event feeds a Slack "Send Message To A Channel" action.


The run details show the first step completed and the run marked as succeeded, which is how you confirm a flow fired before you trust it. Swap Figma in as the trigger and the structure is identical.


Build the audit first, then the alerts, and test each by checking the run log rather than assuming delivery.
